newsitem.title: UK: Algeria, Middle East cited in sugar freight orders.
newsitem.headline: Algeria, Middle East cited in sugar freight orders.

text.p: Middle East and north African end-users were the main feature in Wednesday's new business on London's sugar freight market, shipbrokers said.
Algeria proved a popular destination and featured in two of the day's new orders.
Genoc quoted for 5/6,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Poland to Algeria for prompt shipment dates and trade house E D & F Man for 15,500 tonnes in bulk from east coast Mexico for April 20/25.
Man was also open for 9/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from north France to Umm Qasr for prompt.
Lorico issued two new orders for bulk sugar on the Cuba to Alexandria route. It quoted for 13,000 tonnes for April 20/25 and a further 17,000 tonnes for May 15/25.
Mauritius Sugar Syndicate entered the market with an enquiry for 15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar on its usual run from Port Louis to London for May 5/10.
Shipbrokers said the only firmer business reported came from Booker, said to have fixed 6,000 tonnes from St Kitts to UK/Nantes for the end of April.

Lloyds Shipping Intelligence reported that the Cyprus-flagged bulk carrier Theodoros S. is to complete transhipment of its cargo of 20,000 tonnes of raw sugar on April 16, after which the vessel will go for repairs.
London's May futures contract saw a hefty physical delivery of nearly 90,000 tonnes of sugar from British, Dutch, German and Spanish ports.
The equivalent Paris contract saw a physical delivery of 5,850 tonnes of sugar into Immingham.
Taiwan is to tender on April 22 in New York to buy 30,000 tonnes of raw sugar for arrival between June 5 and 20. The tender will be by invitation only.
